cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a hand-woven strip-cloth gown (riga/boubou style) with embroidered "two knives" (aska biyu) motifs, a traditional West African garment type worn by Wolof and neighboring peoples, consistent with the claimed ethnicity.

physical.title: gown; tobe
physical.summary: Gown (tobe, boubou, riga), part of a three-part costume composed of a cap, gown and trousers. With oblong shaped body with broad sleeves flared towards the top. Composed of 72 narrow strips, uniformly woven from strips of the same fabric as Af1983,23.6.a. A pocket has been sewn to the front, and both front and back have been embroidered in a white cotton thread. The embroidery is in the ‘two knives’ (aska biyu) pattern, using chain and buttonhole eyelet stitch; there is a large spiral at the front and another on the back. The knives themselves are embroidered on top of extra pieces of cloth that have been cut to shape. The gown is hemmed by hand around the neck and sleeves and the garment is lined with machine-woven cotton.
